title: 17-year-old charged in Legion Field shooting that killed 19-year-old

 BIRMINGHAM, Ala. — A 17-year-old has been arrested and charged with murder and possession of a machine gun conversion device in connection with a shooting near Legion Field that killed 19-year-old Dre’Shawn Te’Verious Thomas , Birmingham police said.
 The juvenile male was also charged with possession of a machine gun conversion device, according to a police department news release. BPD said the teen was apprehended in an alley in the 400 block of Fourth Court West as he tried to flee shortly after shots were fired. He will be held without bond at the Jefferson County Jail. Police have not released his name.
 Nine people were shot in two separate incidents near Legion Field on Saturday night , according to police. One person was killed, one victim remains in critical condition and seven others have injuries that are not life-threatening. The injured victims range in age from 19 to 30. Multiple firearms were recovered, BPD said.
 Mayor Randall Woodfin said the shootings happened less than eight minutes apart . He said the first was outside Legion Field’s perimeter, beyond the tailgating area, and the second was across the street near vendors along Graymont Avenue. The Magic City Classic game had ended hours earlier.
 At a news conference Monday, Police Chief Michael Pickett said investigators believed more than one suspect was involved. He said officers had been strategically deployed for the event, but that police cannot have an officer next to every person. The release announcing charges against the 17-year-old did not say whether additional suspects are being sought.
 Woodfin praised the arrest, calling it “a small step toward healing” for the victims’ families and community. He said an arrest cannot bring back a loved one or erase trauma, but knowing the person responsible is no longer on the streets “can allow the healing process to begin.”
 Woodfin also said the shooting “had absolutely nothing to do with the Magic City Classic,” and said the city would continue supporting the event.
 BPD is asking anyone with video or information about the shootings to contact investigators. Anyone with information can call the homicide unit at 205-254-1764 or Crime Stoppers at 205-254-7777. Video can be submitted anonymously through the department’s online portal.
